THE 360° INTAKE

Creator video (thejunglebadger) · Needs permission

Jaspr’s intake is a grate that circles the whole base, so it draws room air in from every direction at once, then pushes it through one large, layered filter: a pre-filter, a particle filter and 1 lb of carbon.

✅ Air in from all sides, through a grate around the base

✅ 114 CFM at fan speed 1, its quietest setting

✅ 33 dBA at its lowest speed

How to read an airflow number.

- Airflow (CFM, or CADR) is how much air the unit moves in a minute. The more air moves through the filter, the more of the room’s air gets cleaned each hour.

- Check it at the speed you’d actually run. Many spec sheets lead with the top speed, which isn’t the one you’ll live with.

- A square-foot rating is that same number divided by an assumed ceiling height and air-change rate. Brands pick different ones, so compare the airflow, not the square feet.

Check it for your room.

Enter your room’s size to see how often Jaspr changes its air. Then pick another purifier to compare, using the airflow its maker publishes: same room, same math.

Your room: 2,000 cubic feet (250 sq ft)

Jaspr · fan speed 1, its quietest114 CFM · 33 dBA
3.4 air changes an hour

The room’s air goes through the filter about every 18 minutes.

Jaspr · top speed340 CFM · up to 58 dBA
10.2 air changes an hour

The room’s air goes through the filter about every 6 minutes.

Compare another purifierSame room, same math
– air changes an hour

Pick a purifier to see its airflow in your room.

The math: air changes per hour = airflow (CFM) × 60 ÷ room volume in cubic feet. A 250 square foot room with an 8-foot ceiling holds 2,000 cubic feet, so Jaspr’s 114 CFM at fan speed 1 changes that air about 3.4 times an hour. A 10-foot ceiling makes it about 2.7. It is a yardstick, not a guarantee: furniture, doors and where the unit sits change how well a room mixes. Rival figures are each maker’s own published numbers, read in October 2026. Makers publish different measures (smoke CADR, airflow rate), so treat the comparison as a guide.

Four things to compare on any air purifier

Airflow where you’ll actually run it, noise at that speed, what it costs to keep running, and whether anyone independent has tested it.

1. Airflow at the speed you’ll run. Jaspr: 114 CFM (smoke CADR) at fan speed 1.

2. Noise at that speed. Jaspr: 33 dBA at its lowest speed.

3. What it costs to keep running. One filter change every six months, swapped in under 30 seconds. Filter subscribers get a lifetime warranty.

4. Independent testing. In a lab test by LMS Technologies, an independent microbiology lab (February 2025), a Jaspr cut airborne mold spores by 97.1% in 1 hour in a 4,000 cubic foot chamber.

What this means for your room.

You don’t need a square-foot rating to size a purifier. Measure the room once: length × width × ceiling height. That’s the volume your air lives in.

At fan speed 1, a Jaspr changes the air in a 2,000 cubic foot room about 3.4 times an hour, at 33 dBA, and it goes up from there when you turn it up.

In a big or open space, start with the room where you spend the most time.

Air changes per hour is a yardstick, not a guarantee. Furniture, doors and where the unit sits change how well a room mixes.
